desc:
This large, dusty road, running from the east to the west, is paved with badly
worn bricks and stones reduced to mere pebbles, to allow large wagons to travel
upon it. The road seems to have been well-used once upon a time. Dry, barren
plains lie in all directions.
name: Ancient Broken Road

desc:
This wide road finds its way from north to west. Paved with stones and bricks,
travel by large and heavy wagons would still be possible despite the obvious
lack of maintenance. The road runs through sloping, barren fields that stretch
out as far as the eye can see, save for the rock wall cliff that looms over the
road to the northwest. The only forms of vegetation nearby are small patches of
dry grass or the occasional thorn bush or small, misshapen tree.
name: Ancient Broken Road

desc:
The ancient, broken road slowly curves its way from the north to the south. The
road is paved with large bricks and broken stones, allowing large wagons to
travel upon it. A steep, rock wall looms over the road to the north and the
west. The road has been built slightly higher than the surrounding plains to the
southeast, allowing excessive rainwater to flow away. The steep cliffs to the
north and west do not allow passage.
name: Ancient Broken Road

desc:
The road runs to the north and the west through barren fields that stretch out
in all directions, save for the sharp spur that looms over the road to the
northwest. The fields are covered with sparse patches of brown, dry grass, and
the occasional small, prickly bush. The road, however, is built on soft sand,
paved with large bricks and broken stones, allowing heavy wagons to travel. A
few clusters of small flowers grow by the side of the road and expand to the
south.
name: Ancient Broken Road

desc:
Curving from north to south, this large and dusty road cuts through rock walls
on the east and west sides. The cut that this road runs through does not allow
travel to the east or west. Small patches of grass grow beside the road, whilst
the road itself is paved with many bricks and stones, reinforcing it. Every here
and there a small thicket of thorn bushes can be spotted, growing at the side of
the road.
name: Ancient Broken Road

desc:
This hill rises toward the southeast, ending in a sudden cliff. The cliff cannot
be climbed. The ground on this hilltop is filled with dry, brown grass and
rarely some thorny bushes. Small rocks and broken boulders lie scattered on the
hard ground, which is a mixture of clay and limestone. A road can be spotted to
the southeast.
name: Jutting Hill

desc:
This dry, brown hill juts from the southeast toward the northwest, lowering into
flat fields north and west. Most of these barren wastelands are covered with
patches of dark brown, dry, grass. The ground, consisting of what seems to be a
mixture of clay and limestone, is too hard and dry to allow ploughing or any
profitable agriculture.
name: Brown Hill

desc:
This dry, barren hill is covered with brown patches of grass, interspersed with
some small thorn bushes and a few lone trees. The ground drops to level fields
to the west and the hill continues to the north, coming to another hill. The way
east and south is blocked by a cliff too steep to climb down. The cliff
overlooks a wide road.
name: Dry Hill above the Road

desc:
No water flows now, but it appears that at some time in the past a stream ran
here, carving this channel out of the living rock. Though the cliffs to the
south appear to offer no viable route between the plains and the mountain
slopes, this ancient water course cuts back into them, twisting and curving its
way between the valley and the heights above. The rock is fairly smooth, but it
should be possible to travel this way, albeit only with considerable effort.
name: Dry Channel

desc:
A lush valley stretches to the north and west, its floor an ocean of tall, dark
green grasses that wave gently in the wind. Protected to the north by a range of
hills, and to the south by the rising mountains, this vale enjoys much milder
weather conditions than most of the nearby lands. A few scattered broadleaf
trees, and numerous low bushes thrive here, especially nearing the feet of the
cliffs to the south and east, where a dense hedge of thorny shrubs has come to
dominate the landscape.
name: Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff

desc:
A lush valley extends out in all directions save to the south, where it runs
right to the foot of a massive cliff. The mountain spur is only a low footnote
to the Misty Mountains that lie further east, but the cliffs nonetheless afford
this vale a good deal of protection from the harsh weather that blights much of
the rest of the land hereabouts. As a result, the topsoil is thicker and richer
here, supporting not only a thick sea of dark green grass, but also scattered
broadleaf trees, and any number of low shrubs. A dense hedge of thorny bushes
dominates the land at the very foot of the cliffs.
name: Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff

desc:
Something has left giant claw marks across the walls and ceiling of this cave as
it descends, clearly the result of some animal-like excavation. The rocky burrow
continues further down where the stench gets more foul. A filthy and perilous
crack leads out to the west, following a slight breeze.
name: Dark Cave

desc:
Bones and filth covers the ground of this smelly cave that has been excavated
out of the mountain. Giant claw marks can be seen running along the sides of the
walls of the cavern, seemingly in an attempt to expand it. The air is absolutely
foul here and its source seems to be some bedding in the corner.
name: Smelly Cavern

desc:
A few groves of tall trees dot the landscape, utilizing the excellent ground and
ample moisture. The tall grass may hide wildlife, and there are trails worn in
the grass that indicate larger animals make their way around here. The hills to
the north can be reached from here following a sharp ascent and the mountains to
the south rise up some distance away.
name: Lush Valley Nearing the Hills

desc:
The valley is covered by tall grass here with some scattered green, broadleaf
trees growing here and there. Nestling in the shelter of a range of hills that
lies to the north, and a mountain spur to the south, these lands are quite well
protected from the fiercest weather, with the result that vegetation flourishes
throughout the vale.
name: Lush Valley Nearing the Hills

desc:
The valley lies to the west, sheltered by mountains to the south and hills to
the north and east. Long blades of dark green grass dance in the gentle wind,
creating waves that ripple across the vale. To the south, a tall cliff face
marks the starting point of a mountain spur, an offshoot of the Misty Mountains
that dominate the horizon far to the east.
name: Edge of a Lush Valley

desc:
Scattered trees dot the landscape among these rolling hills, growing denser to
the east, where they climb up the slopes of more hills. To the west and
northwest, the hills continue, their grassy slopes receding far into the
distance. As the slopes march down into the valley below, to the south, the
grass becomes much longer, and the vegetation lusher.
name: Grassy Hills

desc:
These plains are slightly raised, with some of the run-off from the nearby hill
and mountain ranges supplying much needed moisture. The vegetation is green and
broad-leaf bushes grow in abundance here. The bushes are hardy, being themselves
the only natural windbreak in a land where the prevailing winds are cruel.
name: Green Brush

desc:
The rolling hills continue to the east, north and west of here, their grassy
slopes stretching off into the distance. Grass grows in abundance in and among
the many large boulders that have come to rest here. Down a gentle slope to the
south a lush valley opens up, covered by tall green grass. And further in the
distance, across the valley, a rocky spur of the Misty Mountains can be seen
towering above everything.
name: Grassy Hills

desc:
In the south the many peaks of the Misty Mountains are visible. Their tall peaks
reaching to the clouds. A lush green valley lies before the mountains and these
rolling hills mark the northern boundary of that lush land. Tumbling down toward
the vale, the slope gradually becomes grassier, and the vegetation much greener.
name: Grassy hills

desc:
Curling with the contours of the lands that lie to the southeast, a stream flows
here from the distant mountains, bringing its cold, clear water to the plains.
The banks to either side are alive with lush green grass and a proliferation of
low bushes. Further off to the west and south, a range of hills can be seen on
the horizon.
name: Meandering Stream

desc:
Lush, green grass can be seen growing along either bank of the stream, whose
waters flow from south to west here. The stream bed is rather more rocky here
than either upstream or downstream, and so the waters run much more rapidly,
dancing and bouncing off the rocks as they go. The water is very cold and
crystal clear, fed from run-offs from the mountain range to the east.
name: Deep Stream

desc:
The waters of a cold, clear stream cut across the plains, flowing here from east
to north. The channel is rather wide at this point, and the water flows by so
lazily that it almost appears not to move at all. The southern bank can be
reached by means of some quick-footed action over some slippery looking
boulders.
name: Lazy Stream

desc:
The plains here are a collection of tall green grasses. It is obvious that the
stream feeds into here, as the ground has a slightly marshy feel to it. Water
collects in footprints left here. A stream flows past this field to the east and
north. To the south the ground becomes harder as it meets the slope of a hill.
To the west the plains continue until they meet hills.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
These hills descend rapidly to the north and east, while they rise steadily to
the south and west. The land here is a sea of soft, green grass that stretches
all the way down the hillside to meet what appear to be lush plains that lie to
the north.
name: Grassy Hills

desc:
A narrow tunnel, extending about fifteen feet from an opening in the ground,
leads onto an enlarged burrow. Dug into the red-brown soil, the walls, floor and
ceiling are earthen, and are reinforced naturally by a proliferation of tangled
roots. Though this is obviously a den of some sort, there is no sign of bones,
fur, or any kind of animal activity.
name: Warm Den

desc:
A small field can be seen over a slight rise here, while the landscape descends
to the north. The slopes continue to roll further in the other directions. This
hillside is covered with a scattering of small trees and low brush, that are
just enough to offer scant protection against the winds and rain, but not
sufficient to afford any real shelter from the elements.
name: Grassy Hills

desc:
The lands here are parched, despite their location between a lush stretch of
fields lying near a waterway to the north and east, and a band of grassy hills
crossing the land from southeast to northwest, which passes by not more than a
couple of miles from here. In this area, only a few low, tussocks of dull, dry,
yellow-brown grasses have managed to survive.
name: Arid Plains

desc:
This part of the stream at first glance appears quite deep, but upon closer
inspection the bottom silt can be made out quite clearly. The banks can be seen
in the distance. The water is very cold and clear as it runs by swiftly. The
occasional school of minnows flits by and larger darker shapes can be discerned
which can only be larger fish. Plains can be seen to the east and west, and
beyond them hills which eventually join a large mountain range to the south.
name: Shallow Crossing

desc:
The grasses turn a boggy carpet to the north and east where they draw closer to
a stream, and diminish in health to the south. The landscape is remarkably flat
in this region, though some miles to the south a range of hills rises up from
the plains. To the east, the Misty Mountains dominate the horizon.
name: Marshy Ground

desc:
The water is crystal clear here with several large boulders providing some deep,
and almost still pools near to either bank. Flowing from the south, the waters
turn westward here, but the current is too languid to undercut the bank too
much. Far to the south, beyond the dry plains, hills join a rocky mountain
range.
name: Quiet Stream

desc:
Green fields of knee-high grass spread out all around as far as the eye can see.
A gentle stream that flows by to the south and west is the only visible feature
anywhere at all close by in this flat country. There are little or no sounds, or
visible evidence of wildlife. Rising up, far in the southeast, the faint, yet
distinct shape of a mighty mountain range reaches towards the sky.
name: Field by a Stream

desc:
These green hills descend quickly to the north and south, making passage not
viable in those directions. The stream to the south provides enough moisture to
sustain the healthy mixture of tall grass and wild grains that flourishes across
this meadowland. The brown heads of wild grains nod gently with each breath of
wind, and small animals are barely glimpsed as they use the thick vegetation as
cover from their predators.
name: Hills by a Stream

desc:
The grasses and small brush merge together making this area very green. There is
a slight elevation to the land which gives the appearance of several small
hills. These gently rolling lands stop abruptly to the east at a crevice, and to
the west some green hills loom in the distance. A taller variety of grass
becomes dominant to the south, perhaps fed by the nearby stream.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
The hills here grow some bushes and small trees that become increasingly greener
the further east it extends. From a marshy area to the east a smell of stale
water emerges. There are grasslands to the south, and to the north a small
stream can be seen. The hills continue off to the west.
name: Rolling Hills

desc:
The fields continue here with short, green grasses. The grass grows low to the
ground and can hide only small animals. The wind blows through the grass and a
rippling among the field can be seen as well as heard. The fields continue on to
the east. In the south, an impassable thicket of brushes block the way.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
The ground here is quite alive with grasses and occasional trees. Some rocky
ground is apparent to the north, and to the south the plant growth is noticeably
higher than here, probably maintained by a stream that flows idly in the
distance. To the west, the ground rises sharply at some grassy hills.
name: Fertile Fields

desc:
The stream that flows by to the west has lent its life-giving waters to this
part of the plains, making the lands lush and green. Large, broad-leaf bushes
compete with a sea of tall grass to define the landscape here. Far to the south
a range of hills cuts across the horizon, while to the east the Misty Mountains
dominate the vista.
name: Brush-covered Plains by a Stream

desc:
The ground is uneven here, filled with stones and boulders. The soil seems quite
fertile in the area, and there grows some grass and bushes here. Some of the
taller plants and small trees look trampled, cut, or torn, perhaps by some
animals. The fields continue to every direction.
name: Trampled Fields

desc:
The fields here are not on level ground. The grasses that cover this area are
smaller in variety and completely cover the grounds. To the south there is a
sound of water faintly trickling as the fields meet a creek. There is a crevice
on the ground to the west, which prevent travelling in that direction. A field
of taller grass lies to the north.
name: Rolling Grasslands

desc:
The land is covered by short grasses which ripple when the wind blows through
it. There are grassy fields to the west from here and the large bank of a stream
can be seen to the north. The sound of water running along a stream can be heard
in the distance.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
The fields here are lush and green, fed by nearby streams. The moisture in the
soil continues to the north where a smell of stale water pervades. Deep and
muddy marsh ponds block the way to enter the marshes. To the east and west the
grassy fields continue. There are some rolling small hills to the south.
name: Grassy Fields

desc:
There is little in the way of vegetation in this area but the occasional tree
can be found having taken hold on the banks of the stream. The roots of the
trees have dug down and across, reaching out from the walls of the banks to dip
into the fresh running water below. Piles of debris and soil gathered by the
flow of the water through the plains have become tightly packed against the
tangled mess of the outstretched roots. The water itself has begun to grow muddy
and dirty from its contact with the topsoil of the land. As it travels past this
near blockage, the water gathers speed, as it heads towards a series of small
falls to the west.
name: The Loseithel

desc:
The quiet stream makes its way westward through the hills and plains. Meltwater
that originated as snow in the distant mountains, the water is still chilly and
so clear that the rock-covered bottom of the streambed can be seen perfectly. An
expansive grassland stretches out to the south and hills are visible directly to
the north.
name: The Loseithel

desc:
The bridge above is covering some of the sky here, and occasionally sounds of
someone walking there are audible. The stream is clear and chilly here, formed
from meltwater that is carried from the distant mountains in the east, to meet
with the Bruinen, far to the west. Flatlands border the stream to the south,
where the bridge connects to the ground some feet above the stream.
name: Under a Covered Bridge

desc:
The low bank of the stream to the north appears to flood these lowlands on a
frequent basis as the ground is thick with mud, and water is standing in several
places. The musty smell of stagnant water hangs heavily in the air and there is
a faint hum as tiny insects swarm over the pools.
name: Marshy Lowlands

desc:
A bridge has been constructed to the north crossing the river in a narrow spot.
The ground here is waterlogged, with several sizeable pools of standing water
that have become quite stagnant. The air has a musty, unwholesome smell and the
environment has become an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes and other small
insects.
name: On the Bank of a River

desc:
The bridge underfoot is composed of logs and bundles of branches lashed
together. Dirt has been rubbed into the cracks to form a sort of clay helping
insulate against the water. The hides of various animals have been strung
together above the bridge. They form a tunnel of some sort. Although stretched
as tight as possible, they sag at the midpoint between supporting poles which
have been driven into the bridge.
name: Covered Bridge over Loseithel

desc:
Planks of wood and all manner of other types of foliage have been tightly bound
together to create this bridge. A canopy of animal pelts sewn together is
stretched overhead supported only by stakes periodically set along the path.
name: Covered Bridge over Loseithel

desc:
There is a substantial drop-off to the south where the bank of the stream has
collapsed, perhaps adding risk to any attempt to travel in that direction. The
surrounding lands to the north are low and contain little in the way of
vegetation except for an abundance of coarse grass that covers the ground.
name: Hilly Bank of a River

desc:
East and west the hills continue, while to the south a wide stream cuts across
the countryside. The river side of the hills appear to be flooded with some
frequency, the floodwaters arising from the stream. Tall clumps of grass,
interspersed with reeds, grow in the muddy earth. To the west the rear of a
run-down cottage can be seen.
name: Muddy Hills by a River

desc:
There is a good view of the lands to the south of here. The river flows joyfully
down below the hill, the descent to the river is very steep making the climb not
possible. There are some rocks jutting out of the hills, and there grow only
some small brushes and a few pine and ash trees.
name: Hills by a River

desc:
This field is nearly covered by large boulders and gravel. Little of the once
fertile grasses that have grown here can be seen now. The dust that is kicked up
by the wind scatters the small pebbles that lie here, giving this field a barren
appearance. Grasses have sprung up to the east and south, whilst to the west
hills, similar in appearance to this field, can be seen. The field of rocks
continues north.
name: Rocky Fields

desc:
Short, green grasses grow in abundance here on the flat landscape. Some boulders
and other rocks have come to rest here, and the grasses and moss have almost
overtaken all but a few. The flat grassland continues to the east and south.
More rocks, larger than those here, have come to a rest to the north and west.
name: Flatlands

desc:
The plains are covered with small patches of dried-out, brown grass. Some
thickets of thorny bushes lie scattered around in the fields. The ground is
hard, leaving any form of agriculture out of the question. An ancient, broken
road lies to the north and west, slowly curving through the sloping plains.
name: Barren Plain at the Road

desc:
The hills here are composed mainly of red dirt, broken stone, rough scrub brush
and sparse grass. To the north lies an ancient road. Passage west seems to be
impossible, adding to the somewhat dismal nature of the landscape. To the east
once more lie plains, while to the south are yet more hills.
name: Hills near a Road

desc:
On these arid plains nothing but the hardiest grass can survive. The bleak land
stretches out far to the south and west as a broad shelf, hardly wavering in its
depth or height. This same shelf prevents passage south. To the north an ancient
road cuts its path east and west across the shelf, bordered on the north by a
low ridge.
name: Plains near a Road

desc:
Small thickets of tangling thorn bush are dotted across the dry brown grass in
these billowing fields. The ground is hard and infertile, composed of clay and
limestone. A road can be spotted in the north, crossing the wide plains that
dominate the landscape. Far to the east the white peaks of a mountain range
reach their jagged fingers towards the sky, creating a magnificent backdrop for
the rugged looking camp located in the plains to the northeast.
name: Billowing Fields near a Road

desc:
Dry brown grass sprouts out of the red-brown earth which composes the billowing
fields rolling down from the southeast. Far apart small thickets of tangled
thorn bush give little shelter from the elements or a prying eye. In the north
more plains stretch towards the ancient, broken road, and far off on the eastern
horizon the peaks of a mountain range reach toward the sky.
name: Bleak Plains

desc:
Weak torchlight flickers along the northern and southern walls of this high
east-west tunnel. Some large boulders block parts of the tunnel at intervals,
casting dark shadows along the way and lending the tunnel a very ominous
atmosphere. A very faint roaring noise comes from somewhere to the east.
name: Ominous Tunnel

desc:
This cavern's ceiling is so high it cannot be seen in the darkness. Around the
walls are dim torches striving to light this vast space. On the west end, a
stairway has been carved into the rock, vanishing upwards. Dominating the
southern wall is a massive stone door, carved with foul glyphs. The floor is
strewn with old debris and broken weaponry; evidence of battles long ago or
perhaps just abandoned junk.
name: Lofty Cavern

desc:
This low, vaulted tunnel snakes its way north and south. The chipped ceilings
and walls show signs of crude toolwork. To the north, a heavy stonedoor rests,
engraved with foul glyphs and a leering goblin with twisted eyes and lolling
tongue. On the west wall, a smaller, dark stonedoor is outlined with skulls of
various sizes. The handle looks like bone.
name: Low Roofed Tunnel

desc:
The floor of this cavern is worn smooth and has probably seen much use to reach
its current state. The long passage slopes between two openings; the one higher
up is shrouded in darkness while the lower one seems lit by the same scattered
torches on the walls that sets this cavern in a dim, flickering glow.
name: Long Slope

desc:
A series of sharply sloping caves run from the surface down deeper into the
roots of the Misty Mountains. The caves shown signs of being roughly hewn in
places, apparently to widen them and ease travel for large bipeds of unknown
origin.
name: Sloping Caves

desc:
Softly glowing moss clings gingerly to glistening stalagmites along the weaving
stone pathway. Above, luminescent lichen tattoos the various stalactites
protruding from the damp cavern ceiling. Dripping water echoes throughout the
chamber. A glowing path slopes down into darkness.
name: Glowing Cavern

desc:
This high vaulted cavern spans hundreds of yards in every direction. Stalagmites
and stalactites spring from floor and ceiling, and a quiet, dark pool of still
water lies in the centre of the cavern. The walls of this cave are blanketed
with brightly glowing green mosses, and beds of the same moss cover the slick,
wet ground.
name: Luminous Cave

desc:
A dark tunnel with arched ceilings snakes its way to the north and south amongst
rubble and debris. Some tiny stalactites can be see hanging from the ceiling on
the right side of the tunnel where water is slowly seeping out of the
surrounding rocks. The muddy walls of the tunnel show signs of the crude chisels
that were used to expand it.
name: Low Roofed Tunnel

desc:
This chamber is lined with bulbous rock walls worn smooth by countless years of
dripping condensation. Small droplets cling to every available surface. To the
east, a crude outline of a door is the only break in the otherwise solid stone.
An awful stench wafts in from the south, indicating something vile lies that
way.
name: Dark Dungeon

desc:
The slick walls of this chamber are marred only by the massive iron rings set
into the rock. Each is as wide as a horse, and likely almost as heavy. Their
only use seems to be as an anchor to chain up some immense beasts. The iron is
covered in thick scratches, apparently the result of the prisoners attempts to
gnaw their way free.
name: Dank Dungeon

desc:
A pile of every sort of horror covers this corner of the cavern. Rotten food,
old shoes, and every other sort of refuse are cemented together by noxious paste
of excrement. An occasion foot or finger can be seen mixed in with the rest the
filth. The air is thick with a ghastly stench that threatens to turn even the
strongest of stomachs.
name: Rotten Refuse Heap

desc:
The floor of the cavern gradually descends into a watery pit in the southwest
corner. The water covering that corner is black as pitch, covered in bubbles as
large as a man's head. It is entirely opaque, providing ample covering for
whatever vile creature might be lurking below.
name: Wet Pit

desc:
The eastern side of this low-roofed tunnel is covered in stalactites and
stalagmites that were formed by water slowly seeping out of the surrounding
rock. Natural mineral pigments, ranging in colour from ochre to yellow, can be
seen on the tunnel's walls as it snakes its way to the north and south.
name: Low-roofed Tunnel

desc:
An old mine was operating here, as evidenced by a large pile of rubble and some
heavy pine timbers that have been set into the tunnel as braces. This low
vaulted tunnel can be seen snaking its way north and south. The old mine leads
upwards into a dark cavern accompanied by a slight draft.
name: Low Roofed Tunnel

desc:
Ensconced torches line the walls of this cavern, casting dancing shadows along
the ceiling. The wide floor slopes downward toward a tunnel from which the
continuous rushing sound of water emanates. Tunnels lead to the north and west
into darkness.
name: Torchlit Cavern

desc:
A crudely made stairwell ascends at the western end of the tunnel accompanied by
a foul draft. The tunnel has otherwise been shaped by crude tools into a
corridor that would allow two men to pass side by side. The eastern end of the
tunnel expands out into a cavern.
name: Sloping Tunnel

desc:
A series of wide caverns runs east and west. The stone walls show evidence of
toolwork, crudely carved where the caverns narrow, possibly to make passage
through here possible at all. The cavern floors are dusty and dry, with
footprints in the dirt.
name: Wide Cavern

desc:
This rather long cavern has a wide gap in the ceiling exposing it to the open
sky. A mossy pool of water has collected in the middle of it. To one side is a
crudely fashioned wooden rampart. Scattered in a loose u-shape around the
fortification are large stones to form an extra obstacle, perhaps.
name: Goblin Lookout

desc:
This wide, grey cavern is rather undistinctive. The walls are reasonably smooth
and loose rocks are scattered about here and there. A crudely carved stairway is
chipped into one of the cavern walls, leading up to a large stone which may be
rolled aside.
name: Empty Cavern

desc:
This chamber looks like it was carved out of the rock, the walls are too even to
be natural. An assortment of weaponry and armour has been put here, hanging from
pegs, sitting in weapon racks, or squeezed into cabinets. It is, in short, an
armoury. Judging from the quality of the equipment found here, it is not
maintained by someone who is too keen on quality and keeping things in good
condition.
name: Small Armoury

desc:
The series of caverns running from the west comes to an end then splits off into
a pair of tunnels branching north and south. The northern tunnel slopes
downward, while the southern route terminates in a winding spiral stair. A
simple guardpost seems to have been set up at this junction, with simple
furniture and an empty rack attached to a wall.
name: Cavern Crossing

desc:
A long procession of roughly hewn stairs winds up and down; hundreds of steps
lost in darkness. The stairs are crudely tooled but also made smooth by time and
evident travel. These caverns have been inhabited by something or another for
many long centuries.
name: Spiral Stairwell

desc:
Wet slime slowly ooze down the walls, gathering in shallow pools on the cavern's
floor. The small cave, little more than a recess in the rock, stinks of decaying
plant life. The air is still, thick, and humid. The ceiling is high and the
source of the watery muck is hidden in the gloom above.
name: Wet Recess

desc:
A spiralling staircase leads upwards into a round vertical tunnel, with no end
in sight. The cavern around the staircase looks like it has been expanded, the
walls show signs of being crudely hewn to widen them. Both the stairs and the
floor of the cavern are worn smooth.
name: Spiral Stairs

desc:
A wide tunnel slopes downward, winding back and forth as it descends to the
south. The tunnel is easily broad enough for several goblins to walk side by
side, and the floor and walls of the tunnel show signs of crude chiseling as if
it has been widened on purpose.
name: Sloping Tunnel

desc:
A foul odour fills the air here. The moist cavern walls are coated with a slimy
grey-green fungus, clearly the source of the malodorous stench. Green slime
drips from the cavern ceiling and walls; the muddy floor is wet and slick.
name: Dank Cavern

desc:
A pillar of rock, as broad as three full-grown trolls, dominates the centre of
this nearly circular chamber. Fungal growth covers the pillar entirely, lending
it a brown-green hue. The air is motionless, chill, and oppressively damp.
name: Dank Cavern

desc:
Three tunnels, each oddly distinct, intersect at a round chamber. To the east,
the passage is lined with phosphorescent moss so that the apparently smooth rock
beneath cannot be seen. In contrast, greenish-brown growth obscures a twisting
tunnel to the north. Southward, however, the walls are dry and appear almost
polished, as if delved by hand rather than natural in origin.
name: Dank Cavern

desc:
A thin layer of slimy mildew covers the walls and floor of this tunnel, which
slopes downward from the east and narrows abruptly into an impassable crack to
the west. Water oozes slowly from the ceiling and down the walls. The air is
cold and damp, and the footing is slick and treacherous.
name: Slimy Dead-End

desc:
This chamber hosts a thriving population of varied fungi. Bulbous toadstools
crowd in patches on the floor and phosphorescent mosses shimmer along the smooth
rock walls. Hidden beneath the proliferation of fungi are indistinct piles of
rot in many forms of unclear vegetal or animal origin. A narrow, twisting
passageway exits to the west.
name: Fungal Profusion

desc:
A smooth, polished tunnel leading in from the north suddenly changes directions
as it meets a natural opening in the rock running westward. All signs of
construction halt at this corner, as if the delvers' plans were ruined in
likewise abrupt manner. Faint, steady warmth wafts from further down the tunnel
to the west.
name: Tunnel Elbow

desc:
This broad chamber along an east-west tunnel is apparently used by goblins for
training in combat. A small arena surrounded by stakes strung with leather
thongs lies north of the central passageway, whereas several archery targets are
set up to the south. Bloodstains and scattered bones reveal that restraint is
not always a part of goblin combat exercises.
name: Combat Chamber

desc:
A large tunnel running east-to-west broadens as it branches into a barracks to
the north and smithy to the south. Goblin fletchers have taken up residence in
this part of the cave, evidenced by bone arrowheads and wooden shafts, and
animal sinew lying along the southern wall. Loose bundles of arrows and crude
bows rest at the entrance of the barracks, ready to be taken up at a moment's
notice.
name: Fletcher's Chamber

desc:
All available space in this low, broad chamber is devoted to bedding of various
sorts. Furs, crude mats, and piles of moss lie strewn haphazardly, yet no spot
of the rock floor beneath is visible. The floor space has apparently proven
insufficient, as several hammocks hang from pegs in the walls and ceiling. Faint
warmth and the scent of smoke wafts from the south, a possible reason for the
overstuffed popularity of these sleeping quarters.
name: Cramped Barracks

desc:
A tunnel entering from the east slopes suddenly upward to pass through a narrow
crack no more than a few feet wide. Crude stairs have been carved into the rock
at irregular intervals, sufficiently shallow for goblin-sized legs. The natural
bottleneck of this tunnel affords a strong defensive position. Arms and
supplies, including many crude bows, line the walls.
name: Watchpost

desc:
Ash and soot blacken the walls of a low, broad chamber. Weapons and armour in
various states of construction and repair are strewn about the room. Along the
southern wall, a gentle depression holds hot coals for a smithy's work. A
natural chimney extends upward through the rock, making for a convenient egress
for the smithy's fumes, revealing uncharacteristic ingenuity on the part of the
goblins that use this chamber.
name: Sooty Smithy

desc:
This rocky chamber resembles a funnel, with steeply sloping sides converging
toward a crude staircase that descends eastward from its bottom. The ceiling
dips downward following the shape of the floor below. An oppressively dark
tunnel winds away from the southern entrance to the chamber.
name: Sloping Passage

desc:
A tunnel with pitch-black walls bends around a protruding obsidian rock
formation along its north-eastern wall. The obsidian is run through with grey
streaks of some unknown impurity. Scratches along the otherwise smooth stone
indicate where some creature attempted, but then gave up on liberating this
stone from the rocky walls.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
A narrow tunnel bends as it runs beneath a ceiling of hard, smooth obsidian. A
failed mine that would have run north cuts off suddenly beneath a cascade of
rubble. Several other attempts to extract minerals from the walls are also
evident along the tunnel, these more quickly abandoned.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
This tunnel makes a sharp and sudden bend from east to north. The sheer
blackness of the walls would make this abrupt turn a rather unpleasant surprise
for any who would carelessly dash along this passageway. Sundry supplies spill
out of a deep recess in the southern wall.
name: Sharp Bend

desc:
Piled on either side of a central walkway are stacks and stacks of broken or old
weapons, armour, goblin clothing as well as general refuse. Some of the items
have spilled out onto the path, making fast travel here dangerous. The footpath
leads from the west to a rough-hewn stairway leading down.
name: Scrap Heap

desc:
The floor of this tunnel slopes slightly downward from east to west. The passage
is increasingly covered in dust and small stones. The tunnel seems to be very
old and to the east heavy timbers support the ceiling.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
A swiftly flowing torrent, dark and freezing, carries from the south to the
north through a large, water-worn opening in a slate-grey wall before vanishing
into unknowable depths. A crude path leading up has been hewn out of the bare
stone on the western rockface.
name: Freezing Torrent

desc:
A swiftly, sweeping icy stream courses from south to north here, filling half
the chamber with a chilly, dark liquid. The strange thing is how silent the
river is flowing. To the east, a black eddy swirls into a deep pool.
name: Dark Stream

desc:
Nourished by the meltwater of the Misty Mountains towering up steeply to the
east, green grass overtakes the hard rock of the slopes. The grassland rolls
ever up and down, each decline giving a little shelter against the elements. All
over the small tracks of wildlife run irregularly, suddenly ending or starting,
sometimes with a tiny hole in the ground.
name: Rolling Plains below the mountains

desc:
The ground becomes harder and higher as it draws closer to the mountains in the
east, making it hard for the grass to grow. Some tougher thorn bushes and shrubs
are scattered among the fading grass, seemingly having little trouble surviving
in this harsh hill environment. A small stream twists through the lands to the
west.
name: Hill at the Edge of the Plains

desc:
With a swamp just to the west, this field is flat, damp and a bit smelly at
times. Low lying areas have wetland plants growing in it, and the grass rising
from the red soil is thicker than in other parts of the region. Even the wiry
brush seems healthier and more robust. Still, it is an area that offers little
of interest or even value. To the north some hills rise breaking the view, while
a river flows to the northwest.
name: Dank Field

desc:
A hill covered in rough brush and grass rise overlooking the river and plains.
Passage south and west is blocked by the steep river banks. To the north more
bleak plains as are typical of the region can be seen, while heading south
offers even more of the same kind of plains.
name: Hills by a River

desc:
Having reached the vast plains of this flat land, the stream flows at a more
languid pace in its journey to the northwest. The stream bends westwards, where
vast plains spread out as far as the eye can see. To the south, a swamp forms a
border where water and plains meet.
name: Meandering Stream

desc:
Slowly the stream wends its way through the wilderness making a lazy bend here
to the north. On its banks grows a rough green grass, mixed with small thorn
bushes. To the east rise the foothills of the Misty Mountains and to the north
and west an expanse of rolling grasslands spreads out. Flowing water has eroded
the banks to the south, blocking all travel in that direction.
name: Bend in a Stream

desc:
At this southern end of the river, plains turn to swamp, offering a haven for
all sorts of creatures who love marshy areas. To the east and west lie more
plains, while the river flows north and west for some distance. Looking
northeast, one can see several hills breaking the monotony of the landscape.
name: Swampy Plain

desc:
The ground becomes harder and rougher as it draws closer to the mountains in the
east, making it hard for the dry, brown grass to grow. But some tougher thorn
bushes and shrubs are scattered among the fading grass, seemingly having little
trouble surviving in the harsh environment. A small stream makes its way through
the landscape to the north, cutting the river bank in such a way as to block
passage. To the south lie hills, while swamps form to the east, and plains
continue far to the west.
name: Dried Grassland

desc:
Small patches of bare earth mix in with the occasional stone in these sparsely
vegetated grasslands. The ground is hard and infertile, composed of red-brown
clay and limestone. Far to the east a few foothills can be seen, the lower
slopes of the Misty Mountains.
name: Barren Grassland

desc:
These bleak plains come rolling down from the south to the north. There is close
to no vegetation at all here, save the dry, brown grass that grows in patches in
the dusty, red-brown soil. The fields extend ever onwards, and far off to the
east the ever-white peaks of the Misty Mountains reach up towards the sky.
name: Folded Grassland

desc:
The rugged crags rears above the plains below as they climb toward the mighty
peaks of the Misty Mountains. The mountain's teeth rise above the sky, gnawing
at the firmament. Brush and scrub paint the landscape in green and grey.
name: Rising Crags

desc:
These craggy hills are but the foothills of the high peaks looming above the
land to the east and south. Dangerous cracks and nooks in the rock are hidden by
shrubs clinging to every little crack and patch of earth. The land descends to
the west and north; towards numerous lower hills to the west and a
barren-looking grassland to the north.
name: Crags of the Misty Mountains

desc:
The rolling hills are strewn with large clumps of stinging nettle leaves. Some
care must be taken while crossing the hills to avoid brushing up against the
spiny bushes. To the north, fields of grass and brush cover the land between
these hills and a distant river.
name: Hills of Nettles

desc:
Patches of gorse and brush dot the faded landscape, blots of colour amidst an
otherwise colourless land. To the north are featureless plains, and to the south
are hills dusted with brush and trees. Here and there is the scuttle of small
creatures.
name: Gorse-bush covered Hills

desc:
A few thickets of tangled thorn bushes are scattered amid the small patches of
dry, brown grass that cover the plains. The landscape rolls up and down, with a
few large boulders giving scant shelter from the elements. Far to the east a
mountain range reaches up towards the sky.
name: Rolling Wasteland

desc:
Dry, brown grass covers the plains in small patches, with a few thickets of
tangled thorn bushes in between. The landscape rolls up and down, giving little
shelter from the elements. Close to the east a thickets of wiring brush can be
seen, while in all other directions, the vista is dominated by vast fields of
scraggly grass.
name: Folded Wasteland

desc:
These bleak plains all but define featureless. Flat and without any redeeming
qualities, they are an uninterrupted flat area of scrub brush, grass and brown
dirt. To the east, marshes meet the plains, and a twisted combination of mud,
logs washed from the river further east, and dense brush create an area that
cannot be crossed by even the sturdiest dwarf or strongest troll.
name: Fields Bordering a Swamp

desc:
Small thickets of tangled thorn bushes dot the dry, brown grass in these
billowing fields. The ground is hard and infertile, composed of clay and
limestone. To the east lies a swamp, while all other directions show more of the
same, tiresome plains that offer no relief from the elements.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
Here, the river meets the plains and turns them into a swampy mess. Grass and
water loving brush rise above the waterlogged soil, making passage more
difficult. To the west the swamp gives way to plains, while the swamp continues
to the south, and the river continues to flow in a southeasterly direction.
name: Swamp by Some Plains

desc:
Following the altitude of the grassland the stream takes on a mainly northwest
direction, twisting in between small ridges. The vegetation on the banks is
mainly composed of short grass, reed and a few flowers. South and west of here
swamps form along the edge of the river.
name: Twisting Stream

desc:
Cutting its path through the grassland, the stream now turns in a northwesterly
direction, following the contours of the land. The impassable banks are
overgrown with reeds, grass and small flowers. Looking east and north one can
see foothills to the Misty Mountains forming, but in the southwest grassy fields
continue, seemingly forever.
name: Stream through Some Grasslands

desc:
Plains meet river and turn into swampy marshes here. To the north and east lie
more river. To the west are more swamps, with plains and hills visible further
west. Passage south is blocked by dense vegetation and breaks in the terrain.
name: Murky Marsh

desc:
The low plains have been turned into a marsh by the surrounding waterlogged
lands to the north and east. Higher plains to the west and south remain dry, but
cannot be reached through the muck and mire of this area. Here and there swarms
of mosquitoes flit about looking for some unfortunate creature to feed from and
harass.
name: Marshy Field

desc:
These bleak plains continue far to the north and south as well to the east and
west. There is close to no vegetation at all here, save a few patches of dried
brown grass. Small, dried-out rivulets tell of a time long ago when the land was
less parched, but now dusty, red-brown soil dominates the landscape. Far to the
north a road can be seen.
name: Blasted Field

desc:
Dry, brown grass covers the plains in small patches, with a few thickets of
tangled thorn bushes scattered between them. The landscape rolls up and down,
giving little shelter from the elements. Far to the east great white peaks jut
upward into the sky, a spectacular backdrop to the otherwise repetitive fields
that extend all around.
name: Arid Wasteland

desc:
The arid fields stretch out before you, undulating gently as they progress from
north to south. A few tangled thorn bushes can be seen, a contrast to the
never-ending dry brown grass and hard limestone that otherwise dominate the
landscape. Small old dried-out rivulets tell of a time long before, but now the
dusty red-brown soil dominates the area.
name: Billowing Fields

desc:
All bold colour has departed from this land. Paints of grey and sallow yellow
wash the scrub with faded dreams. Still, a few white blooms toss in the breeze,
as the Misty Mountains loom above on the eastern horizon, stretching in an
unbroken line from northeast to southeast, its mighty peaks shrouded in clouds.
name: Faded Heath

desc:
Grey and green dominate the landscape with patches of mottled brush. To the west
the brush clears, and to the east the brush continues, albeit a different hue.
The mighty mountain range known as the Misty Mountains rises to the east,
dominating the view.
name: Grey Heath

desc:
The rolling grey wastelands begin to rise to the west, where a slender goat
trail winds up onto a high ridge that dominates the western skyline. To the
south are more wastes, and to the east, much the same, but spotted with grey
brush and clumps of wiry grass.
name: Barren Wasteland

desc:
Rising high above the surroundings, this ridge wends its way from the northeast
to the south, becoming a high saddleback. Off to the west can be glimpsed a
winding, broken road, grey and forbidding. Barren wastelands lie to the east.
Beyond, a shimmering blue-grey river cleaves the blasted lands.
name: High Ridge

desc:
A ring of hemlocks springs from the brush, their thick green spines filling the
sky like a crown. Amidst the break in the scrub, a strange mushroom fairy ring
mimics the brush. West and east the hemlocks pop amidst the scrub, their small
white flowers in contrast with the drab greens surrounding them.
name: Hemlock Grove

desc:
The low hills are lightly covered with hemlock plants and sparse brush. The
small white flowers of the hemlock plants stand in contrast to the faded greens
of the other plantlife. The great Misty Mountains rise high above to the south
like crowns against the sky.
name: Hemlock-covered Foothills

desc:
The brush here is coloured in blueish-green, thickly clumped, and studded with
nettles. A small cul-de-sac has been created by the dense foliage and towering
peaks to the south. Little shows from the sky, the brush forms a dense hedge
that covers any light from entering.
name: Thick Bluebrush

desc:
These bleak fields roll in a north and south direction, and are covered with
dense, stunted brush that struggle to rise from the barely fertile soil. On top
of a small elevation, a single gnarled tree fights to rise above the unforgiving
ground. From time to time, cold and harsh winds blow down from the mountains
rising far to the east. Badly broken ground prevents any travel south, limiting
options for the weary traveller, while foothills break the landscape closer to
the east.
name: Bleak Fields

desc:
Dry brown grass covers the hill in small patches, protruding through the thin,
red-brown soil. A few thickets of tangled thorn bushes can be spotted in this
unsheltered land. The soil is unfruitful which explains the barren view. Close
to the east lie flatter brush-covered plains. Passage west and south appear to
be impossible.
name: Barren Hill

desc:
Scattered brush and thorny bushes litter the hardened red soil. Fragments of
quartzite are the only things that can be seen jutting up from the rolling hill,
and no shelter is to be seen for miles around. Further off to the east rolling
fields stretches out. Passage to the west is blocked by harsh terrain that
offers no exit. To the south, even more hills rise.
name: Brush Covered Hill

desc:
Miles of featureless, flat terrain spread all around. Here and there grass and
scrub brush manage to find life on the nearly waterless plains. To the far east,
hills can be seen breaking the monotony of the landscape. Dense, interlocking
thickets of brush prevent all travel to the north and east, making this a rather
unpleasant place to be cornered in.
name: Brushy Plains

desc:
Long stretches of empty, grey plains spread out to the north and south
punctuated only by spurts of dark bushes and patches of hardy grass. In the
west, the land rises to a faint trail that leads higher up.
name: Barren Wasteland

desc:
A dusty trail rolls up and down this high ridgeline. Among the rocks and dust
some sprigs of hardy grass maintain a precarious existence in defiance of the
elements. Looking west, a steep incline rises along the horizon. To the east, a
small trail snakes up from dull, grey wastelands below.
name: High Saddleback

desc:
A faint goat trail winds its way from the high ridge to the north down into a
stony vale. Tough, grey-green vegetation clings to the hillsides in patches and
clumps as steep rockfaces prevent movement except along the winding trail.
name: Craggy Hills

desc:
A small valley nestles below the northern craggy hills. Flat, round stones are
scattered across the vale in a variety of shapes and sizes. Tufts of scrubgrass
and nettles poke up between the stones determined to survive the hostile
environment. To the west, a wide plain opens up while beyond, a broad ridge of
hills rises in the distance.
name: Vale of Stones

desc:
The grasses that grow here are shorter than usual, clinging to the ground in
abundance. This keeps them from blowing away and traps their own moisture
securely to the ground. The plains continue to the west and south, while a
wilted and dried field can be found north.
name: Flatlands

desc:
Dry, wilted grasses lie scattered about here. This once thriving field is no
longer fed by water and, as a result, the grasses are desiccated, and dead or
dying. The fallow fields continue onwards north and west. To the south, short
stout grasses, hardier than those found here, grow in abundance.
name: Dry Fields

desc:
This could have once been a thriving field, with healthy plant life and maybe
even produced some crops for hardworking farmers. Now it is only slightly more
than a dry desert. The long wide cracks in the ground harbour dust, dirt and
dead weeds. Little else exists here since it is so dry. The desolate fields
continue to the north, west, and south.
name: Fallow Wasteland

desc:
The ground is hard and infertile, mostly composed of clay and limestone. A thick
layer of dust covers the ground of these arid fields. A ridge ascends to the
south and east, but it allows passage to south. No other landmarks can be seen
across the wide plains, except for the large mountain range that looms in the
distance to the east.
name: Arid Fields

desc:
This field is covered in small stones and pebbles. A landslide probably moved
the covering soil away and left the rocks here. Small bunches of brown grass
spring up between the rocks, however the field is far too filed with stones to
be of any agricultural use. The fields continue in all directions with little
discernible change.
name: Rocky Fields

desc:
The soil is dry and cracked in this place. No moisture reaches here and the dust
is evident. The few scraggly weeds that have grown up from the cracks are little
more than yellowed, dead husks. A single, stunted tree once grew here, but that
has fallen to the ground, cracked and dry as a bone.
name: Dry Wasteland

desc:
The hills here are covered with rocks of every size. The brush and grasses that
squeeze between the stones give this area a sparse appearance. There are rocky
fields to the east and south of here, while there is a bit more vegetation to
the west and little growth to the north.
name: Rocky Hills

desc:
It would be a tremendous feat of nature for any life form to survive prolonged
exposure to the harsh elements in this area. The dusty hills are dry and the
ground is cracked in several places. There are no trees or shrubs to provide
shelter nor is there any water source visible. The hills descend slightly to the
east and continue to the north and south.
name: Barren Hills

desc:
Dry and lifeless, the slightest breath of wind kicks up whirlwinds of dust
across this gritty promontory. The soil lacks any nutrients and is filled with
cracks. An overgrown road lies directly to the west while the fields continue to
the south. Far off in the east the horizon is filled with high jagged peaks
creating the image of a large jaw jutting up from the earth.
name: Lifeless Promontory

desc:
Thin cracks spread out tenuously where the earth has split from the lack of
moisture, and small rocks litter the ground across these desolate fields. The
fields stretch out flat and lifeless to the east, while a steep ridge ascends to
the west and south. An old road is visible to the north.
name: Barren Fields

desc:
Grey and grey and grey. Barren and blasted, these areas are not a place any wise
man might tread. The ground is uneven and the dry earth is cracked in places and
covered with rocky formations in other. To the east, the lands flatten out more
except for a tall rocky formation.
name: Barren Wasteland

desc:
This rocky formation is butting up against the rising Misty Mountains to the
east, but further ascent is blocked by sheer walls of rough stone. The ground
has numerous cracks and crevices, some of which looks to be used as nests by
birds. Westwards, a more gentle slope descends to lower ground.
name: Atop a Rocky Formation

desc:
This outhouse has clearly seen better days -and better users. Now broken down
and reeking of unspeakable filth, it is both the only shelter from the sun for
possible miles around, but also the only place to get a little private relief if
truly needed. There is no real way of telling who might be desperate enough, or
perhaps foolhardy enough to use this building. A stinking pit opens down from
the middle of the building, and a well-worn, creaky door appears to be latchable
for a little privacy.
name: Dilapitated Outhouse

desc:
This foul, stinking pit is full of water, faeces, and other disgusting items
perhaps half a yard deep. The reeking smell seems to rise to the heavens and
there is no real relief from it. Streaks of greenish brown slime line the
crudely dug earthen walls, and the only way back up seems to require getting
covered in that same slime.
name: Stinking Pit

desc:
A dry streambed winds westward as it descends a rugged slope. To the west, steep
ravines and jagged fissures cut into the coarse, darkened rock that comprises
the surrounding mountainous landscape. Southward, sheer rockfaces thrust
ever-upwards towards rugged crags and sharp, broken peaks of various heights.
name: Rocky Incline

desc:
Towards the south, the jagged outline of a natural, rocky maw blends into the
lighter landscape beyond. Darkness progressively replaces light in the depths of
the cave to the north, and only dim outlines of dark, glistening rock can be
seen. The faint drip of liquid lightly echoes across the wide walls and ceiling
of this place, the roof of which disappears into total darkness high above. The
only suggestion of a ceiling existing at all is the tips of rocky teeth hanging
down far enough to barely discern them against the darkness.
name: Cavernous Maw

desc:
Towards the south, the darkness appears to be slightly less dense, as the
occasional small point of light can be seen, suggesting an opening in the
passages far in that direction. The hard, rocky floor of this cave abruptly
slopes downwards to the north, where darkness overtakes any last reflections of
light off the jagged stone walls.
name: Sloping Passage

desc:
The rocky passage continues to the east and west, offering little to no
visibility save where artificial light is offered. However, as if reluctant to
challenge the engulfing darkness, illumination seems to fall short of where the
distance would shine otherwise. Faint drops of water faintly echo across the
uneven walls of rock, which seem to resonate slightly louder to the east.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
Curving northward as the tunnel continues from the west, the darkness seems to
swell thickest in that direction. Downward, the jagged floor begins to descend
rapidly into a veil of shadow, beyond which even the strongest light seems
unable to touch.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
The jagged stone floor gradually becomes more level here, from where it sloped
down unevenly from the passage above. Toward the east, the darkness swells
thickest, indicating the tunnel advances in that direction. Faint sounds of
dripping water can be heard echoing strange patterns across the walls,
occasionally mixed with other strange, unfamiliar noises.
name: Sloping Passage

desc:
Here the cold stone tunnel, with jagged teeth of rock overhead and along the
walls, meets a sudden dead-end. Strewn about the floor are pieces of broken bone
mixed with half-finished and broken tools, crafted from the surrounding hard
stone. The only way out is south, where the darkness seems to wait in welcome
for any light to foolishly challenge it.
name: Tunnel End

desc:
The cold, jagged walls of rock that comprise the walls of this tunnel begin to
narrow slightly towards the south, where the tunnel appears to continue on into
the darkness. Towards the east, the tunnel continues its solemn, cold march into
the blackness.
name: Branching Tunnel

desc:
A narrow tunnel opening lies to the north, where the cold, jagged walls of
dark-coloured stone also comprise the surrounding cave-end here. Upon the ground
lie fragments of shale-like rock, scattered throughout piles of discarded pieces
of bone. What appears to have been a failed attempt at making crude weaponry out
of bone and stone now serves as litter upon the ground.
name: Abrupt Dead-End

desc:
Here, the cold stone walls that largely make up these dark, damp tunnels turns
northward, where the darkness seems to swell into an opening; no sounds or faint
glistens of sharp rock can be seen in that direction, as is present to the east
and south.
name: Tunnel Bend

desc:
Sloping upwards, the ground here becomes ever-scattered with broken sheets of
rock, amongst which several small bones are mixed. As the hard, rocky floor
rises, so the space between the jagged walls become smaller, making for uneasy
travels as the elevation rises. The tunnel bends in from the south, where very
little can be seen in the engulfing darkness that seems to thicken with distance
in that direction.
name: Ascending Tunnel Bend

desc:
Rising from below and to the south, the rocky floor, littered with stones and
the random bones of small creatures, levels out and begins to swing eastward.
While the tunnel walls are much more narrow as it follows the descent, they
begin to widen out the further east one travels. Several rocky protrusions
thrust out from the cave walls, threatening any whom pass close to them.
name: Steep Tunnel Bend

desc:
Descending from above, the stone and bone-laden tunnel floor evens out
momentarily before turning westward, where the view yields nothing but the
awaiting darkness. Toward the west the tunnel expands outwards, jagged fingers
of rock protruding from the stone walls await any unaware travellers.
name: Steep Tunnel Bend

desc:
Ascending from below, the stone and bone-laden tunnel floor evens out
momentarily, before splitting toward the north and south where the view yields
nothing but the awaiting darkness. Small droplets of water drip from the damp
ceiling above, forming a small puddle from which runs a tiny stream downwards,
flanking the rocky descent to one side.
name: Tunnel Fork

desc:
The sound of dripping water is ever-present here, where moisture can be seen
pooling upon the ceiling before dripping into the puddle-covered stone floor
below. From these puddles, small streams constantly flow downward where the
walls of rock disappear under a cold, dark waterline.
name: Watery Descent

desc:
Dripping water and bat droppings merge here to coat a treacherous, slippery,
sloping tunnel. The water has no apparent source besides the ceiling above, from
which it slowly accumulates to fall noiselessly on the guano-softened ground.
The tunnel opens up into a broader cavern to the north and steepens further to
the south.
name: Guano-Slickened Slope

desc:
Unbearably cold water entirely fills this passageway. The channel flows slowly
southward, where it broadens into a larger chamber. The flow is fed by several
narrow cracks up and to the north. One of the cracks broadens into an open air
tunnel above.
name: Chilly Channel

desc:
Icy water fills a large chamber floor-to-ceiling. A slow current, entering from
a channel to the north and exiting through several cracks to the south, gives
the water an even chillier and more dangerous aspect, and no creature not born
to the cold could abide here for very long. Bobbing slabs of ice at the surface
of the water reveal that there is open air above.
name: Chilly Channel

desc:
The strong presence of bats is unmistakable as great mounds of guano and its
accompanying odour fill this expansive cavern. Far above, a broad crack in the
mountainside shows their path of ingress and egress. The floor of the cavern is
fairly level, though mounded here and there with waste. The cave narrows to a
tunnel to the south, and a narrow crack leads downward further into the
mountain.
name: Guano-Filled Cavern

desc:
The rock of this chamber is oddly smooth, rising upward like a bowl from a
shallow depression in its centre. A remarkably straight and level tunnel cuts
northward through a door bordered with weathered runes. Mounds of guano pile
beneath a narrow crack in the otherwise polished ceiling, coating a pile of
rubble that rises up to the crack to create an unintended exit from this room.
name: Befouled Chamber

desc:
A steep tunnel descends from the west to join a larger north-south passage.
Regularly spaced steps lead upward, shallow enough to befit the strides of
dwarves. The floor and walls are smooth and polished, yet dusty with disuse.
However, a few footprints of varying apparent age indicate these tunnels have
not been completely abandoned.
name: Branching Tunnel

desc:
A passageway leading in from the south meets a winding stone staircase that
descends steeply northward. The rough, natural ceiling suggests the builders
simply took advantage of a natural opening in the rock. In several places along
the stairs, deep gouges indicate exploratory mines of ore veins that apparently
proved to be a disappointment.
name: Stone Staircase

desc:
While the tunnel runs almost perfectly straight from this point eastwards, its
floor slopes with frequent changes, and even slight reversals of the grade to a
general trend of a westward descent. The walls of this sloped tunnel are made of
natural rock formations.
name: Sloped Tunnel

desc:
A long, steep staircase zigzags downward along the floor of a natural opening in
the rock, following the slanting cavern as it bends eastward at the bottom. The
cadence of the steps appears best suited for dwarf legs, though the clearance
above the staircase would admit a much larger creature. Broken picks and shovels
rest inside shallow delvings along the northern wall, none of which seems to
have been particularly fruitful.
name: Stone Staircase

desc:
The ruined remnants of a forge line the eastern wall of this large, square
chamber. The bottom half of a massive broken cogwheel rests in a long, narrow
sluice that vanishes beneath a pile of rubble to the north. The shattered pieces
of the forge itself would be scarcely recognisable except for the surprisingly
intact bellows nearby. The only anvils that remain are broken beyond repair. A
vast arcade extends westward from this chamber, and an ornate stone stairway
runs upward and to the south.
name: Shattered Forge

desc:
Water drips through numerous cracks in the ceilings and walls of this chamber,
forming runnels that merge to flow down a set of steps leading to an underground
river below. Stalactites in plenty hang from the ceiling, dripping frequently to
add their contributions to the stream. A squared passage rises upward to the
south.
name: Watery Descent

desc:
An arched hall of magnificently carved obsidian ends abruptly at a great
collapse along the western wall. Fine debris spreads away from the rubble,
covering the broad, meticulously smooth floor. Efforts to break through the
rubble appear to have ended in failure, a story told by crushed remains of both
dwarves and goblins.
name: Collapsed Arcade

desc:
Emerging from a grey rockface to the south through a dark opening worn smooth by
untold aeons of wear, a swift and icy river flows through the wide, open tunnel.
The strong current carries from south to north in a silent race to unknown
destinations. A rough stairway has been cut into the bare slate on the eastern
rockwall.
name: Subterranean River

desc:
Dark, grey waters swirl and eddy here, fed by the current to the west. A gentle
suction pulls the dark water downward in an unstable spiral to an underground
chamber from which a faint glimmer can be seen. Along the edge of the eddy, a
crude path has been chiselled, winding upward to a dark room.
name: Swirling Pool

desc:
A small natural stair leads up into this noisy grotto. The source of the noise
is a a swift subterranean river that can be seen below; its dark grey waters
swirling, rushing, and clamouring. The grotto is incredibly wet with moisture
dripping from the ceiling and misting up from the rushing river current.
name: Noisy Grotto

desc:
The chilly and murky water in this chamber makes it difficult to see more than a
few feet in any direction. Coating the floor is a thick layer of soft, dark
brown sediment. Occasionally, a glimmer shines through the murk.
name: Submerged Chamber

desc:
A small, grubby room is pontooned to the side of the bridge. The floor is a bit
unsteady as it rises and falls in accordance with the river's mood. Mud has been
repeatedly tramped in here, and the wood planks in the walls are largely warped
and discoloured.
name: Guardroom

desc:
This cramped den extends back five or so yards before terminating. Roots fall
from the ceiling of the den and bits of fur can be seen strewn across the
ground. Something large has made its home here and bits of bedding made up of
leaves, grass, and bark have been carefully placed at the end of the den.
name: Dark Den

desc:
This large cavern branches off to the north, south, and east. The stone floor
shows the wear and tear of many goblin claws. On the western wall is inset the
goblin equivalent of a bulletin board. Presumably, it is used to post edicts
from the Chief, patrol duties, shift changes and the latest enemies killed - of
which there are none at the moment.
name: Goblin Junction

desc:
Crude chiselling and chipping have resulted in jagged and craggy walls framing
this passageway. The only smooth thing here is the hard stone floor showing the
wear of much traffic over many years. Passages lead north, south, and west.
name: Crude Passageway

desc:
Several heads, most of them old and little more than bones, adorn the walls of
this long, low-ceilinged tunnel. Several torches, long burnt out, are mounted
alongside the skulls and must have given a ghastly atmosphere to the tunnel when
lit. Most of the heads are human or display the nasty fangs of orc or goblin.
name: Tunnel of Heads

desc:
The western wall of this cave is one of many goblin worksites scattered
throughout the caverns. Recent excavations show where the goblins have dug for
ore or gemstones. The walls are shored up by uneven, roughly hewn timber that
looks anything but stable.
name: Goblin Worksite

desc:
The passageway bends from north to east with a ceiling low enough to make a cave
troll stoop. Running through the dark, craggy stone of the walls are veins of
glossy, black rock with corners and edges deadly sharp to the touch.
name: Gloomy Bend

desc:
In this well-lit and spacious cavern, a huge wooden desk dominates with
authority. Functioning as a guardpost before a wide stairwell set in the eastern
wall, no one gets by without the guards say so. On either side of the stairway
are leering goblin heads of stone, carved to instil fear in the lowly. A couple
of lanterns hang on hooks on the wall opposite the desk, their flames steady and
bright.
name: Security Checkpoint

desc:
In the corner, a wide stairway leads down to a well-lit chamber below. Over the
top of the stairwell is a grinning goblin head. Shields and faded wall hangings
intersperse with glowing torches, denoting this area is of some importance. The
hard stone floor shows scuffs and claw marks leading east.
name: Entrance Hall

desc:
This chamber, connected through empty doorways to the west and south, is large
but sparsely furnished. Some simple benches line one wall and an empty table
stands in front of them. A trophy is mounted on the wall next to the southern
doorway, the remains of a very large humanoid head, but barely recognisable as
such.
name: Crude Chamber

desc:
Large flaming torches brightly illuminate this large cavern. Along the walls
hang shields and dusty tapestries in disrepair. A large rectangular table
dominates the space, cluttered with dirty plates, spilled goblets, and other
signs of recent use.
name: Great Hall

desc:
Fading parchments show rough sketches detailing past plans for raids on a
variety of regional targets. The chieftain of this goblin tribe is obviously
very bold and arrogant. A large square table sits here, holding up a large pile
of these papers.
name: Planning Room

desc:
The east wall is covered with several different sets of rusted, worn out body
armour: chain mail, brigandines, and the like in massive sizes. On the south
wall is a large display of weapons ranging from twin-bladed axes to jagged
longswords to all sorts of crushing devices - all in disrepair.
name: Armoury

desc:
Great braziers mounted on four basalt columns light up every part of this throne
hall, bathing it in a deep, orange glow. Intricate designs carved into the domed
ceiling dance in the flickering light, while dark statues look down upon a
crimson rug that splits the entire cave in half from the doors to the throne.
The attempt at grandeur in this chamber bespeaks an arrogance as large as its
owner, the goblin chieftain.
name: Chieftain's Throneroom

desc:
Wide enough for six goblin troopers to march abreast, this long passage has
fairly low ceiling. Dotting the rough, chipped walls on either side are
flickering torches set in rough metal sconces. The well-trodden walkway curves
from the south to the west.
name: Curving Tunnel

desc:
Many pairs of goblin feet have clawed their way to the east and west. The stone
floor has been pounded by all the foot-traffic. No dust along the walkway
indicates this tunnel has been recently used. Dimly flickering torches line the
walls.
name: Trampled Tunnel

desc:
After resting, eating and enjoying some off-duty time in the caves to the west
and south, this is where small troops form up before moving out on patrol. A
large assortment of weapons and other necessary gear hang on the north wall,
dimly lit by several torches along the walls.
name: Assembly Room

desc:
Various sorts of tables and contraptions are laid out here, designed to
entertain and challenge the goblins in their down time. From throwing knives at
a bloody wall target to claw-wrestling, goblins enjoy what little off-duty time
they can get here. Torch-light spilling in from the east casts gloomy shadows
throughout this cavern.
name: Game Room

desc:
Into the west, north, and east walls, dark recesses have been chipped until a
full-size goblin could fit inside. It looks as if many hundreds of goblins could
sleep in here at the same time. The dank musty odours of goblin breath and body
stench fill the air.
name: Goblin Lodge

desc:
A single long, wide table occupies the central area of this part of an expansive
cavern. Various food items, mostly large wooden plates with meats occupy the
table. Several large mugs stand on the table, or lie on their sides, spilled
contents staining a table that's seen better days.
name: Food Dump

desc:
Hot and musty, this kitchen is dominated by a large pile of rotting meat that
has been stacked haphazardly in one corner. What seems to be a meal has been
prepared over a large pot that absolutely reeks of rot. Various cooking vessels
and tools hang from a low overhead ceiling. A couple of flickering torches
lights the kitchen, if just barely.
name: Goblin Kitchens

desc:
Dingy and dim, this corner of the cavern is cluttered with a few cabinets and
storage lockers lining the walls. Piles of unwashed wooden food bowls are
haphazardly stacked, waiting to be cleaned. A large wooden tub full of nasty
water sits nearby.
name: Cluttered Pantry

desc:
A crudely chiselled tunnel winds back and forth while rising to the south. Broad
enough for several goblins to march side by side, the chipped walls are adorned
with flickering torches interspersed with skulls. To the north, it almost smells
like food is being prepared.
name: Sloping Tunnel

desc:
Though not known for cleanliness, even goblins understand that fouling the
caverns make them unlivable. In the walls and along the baselines, are a series
of small openings and pits for relieving oneself. The stench emanating from
these areas is overwhelming and intense.
name: Goblin Latrine

desc:
Here the cold, jagged tunnels of mountainous rock branch east and west, with the
exception of a nearby rocky ascent upwards. The hard stone walls glisten with a
faint hint of moisture when artificial light is present, which the darkness
readily swallows once removed. In all directions the visibility yields to the
engulfing darkness after only a few feet, as if the light itself knows the
futility of further effort.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
A natural recess extends deep into the wall of a larger tunnel to the north.
This seems to have been considered a convenient location for tossing supplies of
all sorts. Shabby furs, short spears, and poorly maintained armour feature
heavily, with neither rhyme nor reason apparent in their placement in many
sordid piles.
name: Disorganized Alcove

desc:
A vast glacier stretches down from a mountain to the north to end at a chill,
clear lake. Water trickles into the lake from the glacier snout, and several
large chunks of ice float on the surface. Steep, narrow moraines to either side
offer no purchase for any traveller who would wish to continue up the
mountainside.
name: Glacier Lake

desc:
Parallel ridges run across a broad, U-shaped valley, each evidence of a
glacier's retreat. The ridges are shallow and easy to traverse, and are composed
of soil, gravel, and small rocks. The glacier that abandoned this debris long
ago stands to the north at the edge of an icy lake. The deep valley it carved
bends westward as it descends.
name: Recessional Moraine

desc:
A gently rolling till plain covers the floor of a deep, curved valley with
steeply sloped sides. The pebbles, rocks, and boulders that litter the plain
were abandoned long ago in the rapid retreat of a glacier. A careful eye will
note that a faint pattern of parallel curves can be discerned among the debris,
each following the bend of this valley as it descends from east to south.
name: Ground Moraine

desc:
A narrow crevasse cuts through icy walls that extend apparently beyond limit to
heights far above. Numerous cracks run upward along the walls, and long,
precarious-looking icicles extend from jagged points left by fallen ice. The
ground is slick with refrozen meltwater.
name: Narrow Crevasse

desc:
A wide cleft in glacial ice broadens as it runs southward. Here and there, gaps
in the glacier hundreds of feet above reveal glimpses of a sky, and a world
beyond this endless ice. Rubble intermingles with shattered ice blocks to form a
rough but navigable passage.
name: Broad Crevasse

desc:
A nearly vertical slope curves from the north to the east, sloping away from a
pair of peaks high above. The cliff is broken only by a thin shelf no wider than
the breadth of three men. A faint trail is barely visible in the shadowy depths
of a valley below.
name: Steep Mountainside

desc:
A narrow ledge zigs and zags back and forth along the face of a cliff. Its outer
edge is crumbling, leaving great, jagged gaps that leave only a few feet of
passable terrain between a steep slope and steeper drop-off. Debris from the
ledge, boulders, and scree litters the mountainside below.
name: Jagged Ledge

desc:
Smooth, flat rock juts outward from a mountain peak to the north, coming to a
jagged edge where large slabs of rock have broken off to crumble into boulders
strewn along the slope below. Far below, a trail winds back and forth between
this precipice and a similarly steep set of cliffs on the opposite side. A
narrow, rocky ledge descends eastward along the slope of the mountain.
name: Jagged Precipice
